# Hoang–Reed conjecture on cycles with small overlaps

A sequence $C_1,\ldots,C_r$C 1​,…,C r​ of directed cycles has at most one overlap per cycle if, for each $i$i, the $i$i th cycle shares at most one vertex with the union of its predecessors. Hoang–Reed conjecture. Every digraph $D$D with

contains a sequence $C_1,\ldots,C_r$C 1​,…,C r​ of directed cycles such that, for each $i\in [r]$i∈[r],

Conjecture   Every digraph in which each vertex has outdegree at least Image: $ k $ contains Image: $ k $ directed cycles Image: $ C_1, \ldots, C_k $ such that Image: $ C_j $ meets Image: $ \cup_{i=1}^{j-1}C_i $ in at most one vertex, Image: $ 2 \leq j \leq k $.

This conjecture is not even known to be true for Image: $ k=3 $. In the case Image: $ k=2 $, Thomassen proved [T] that every digraph with minimum outdegree 2 has two directed cycles intersecting on a vertex.

This conjecture would imply the Caccetta-Häggkvist Conjecture.

In the other direction, if ${\displaystyle G}$ is ${\displaystyle k}$-degenerate, then an ordering with coloring number ${\displaystyle k+1}$ can be obtained by repeatedly finding a vertex ${\displaystyle v}$ with at most ${\displaystyle k}$ neighbors, removing ${\displaystyle v}$ from the graph, ordering the remaining vertices, and adding ${\displaystyle v}$ to the end of the order.
